superseded_mutable_artifacts_by.reason: Later rapid-approach, organic-canyon, and nonperiodic-canyon milestones intentionally resaved the runnable map, regenerated all three current camera views, and refreshed the generated candidate manifest. The hashes below remain the immutable transmitting-water V2 historical record; the current V3 review owns those mutable artifact hashes.

architecture.runtime_volume: The solver-clipped wet-cell volume core resolves a Colorado-only V2 material instance from the cooked-field identity when the versioned runnable map does not serialize the new override. Newly regenerated maps persist the same material and river-local texture references.
architecture.runtime_detail: The existing smoothed Default Lit mesh becomes a low-coverage hydraulic detail skin. A project-owned Hance flow normal supplies irregular multiscale response, and a project-owned foam-lace mask is multiplied by solver-owned speed and aeration so it cannot paint foam into calm or dry cells.
architecture.capture_water: The non-colliding capture ribbon is now translucent Default Lit water with physical IOR 1.333. Vertex alpha is authored only from already sampled solver depth, wet-bank edge coverage, and aeration; the material scales it by 0.90 and adds no displacement.
architecture.authority_boundary: Both image-generated textures and all material changes are visual-only. Solver fields, wet/dry ownership, curved river coordinates, bathymetry, collision, buoyancy, raft forces, feature forcing, and rapid detection remain unchanged.

live_pie_evidence.diagnostic_scope: The launch-window PIE audit proves runtime carrier activation and map compatibility; it does not prove downstream Hance rapid art or hydraulic calibration.

fixed_camera_comparison.method: Direct RGB means over the lower half of each identical 1280x720 fixed camera, plus full-frame mean absolute channel delta. Values are in 0-255 sRGB. The pre-milestone images were copied to an external immutable review backup before capture.
fixed_camera_comparison.verdict: Retain as a bounded optical improvement: the old dark gray opaque foreground is replaced by transmitting sediment-colored water through which the riverbed and bank geometry remain readable. Horizontal bands, thin-water appearance, duplicate guide and rapid views, and missing rapid-scale whitewater keep photoreal acceptance closed.

validation.fixed_camera_capture: RaftSim.M9.FColoradoHanceWaterCapture passed 1/1 and wrote all three saved-map cameras
validation.native_runnable_map_audit: RaftSim.P4.RiverMapLoads.L_Hance passed 1/1 after the acceptance contract was updated to recognize Colorado as a retained wet-cell volume-core river

remaining_photoreal_defects: Horizontal cross-river bands remain visible because a material cannot reconstruct continuous hydraulics from the coarse cooked visualization field.
The transmitting foreground is visually thin and too riverbed-dominant; physically credible suspended-sediment depth, extinction, caustics, and reflection balance remain incomplete.
The fixed guide-seat and solver-rapid cameras currently resolve to duplicate views, so the evidence does not independently frame the rapid crux.
Foam remains sparse and lacks convincing crests, holes, rollers, entrained-air volume, spray, mist, and rock-contact plumes.
Canyon walls remain visibly terraced and lack surveyed Hance strata, alcoves, talus, erosion cuts, and bank breaklines.
Ground cover, shrubs, riparian structure, woody debris, and boulder variation remain procedural, sparse, repeated, or ecologically unreviewed.
Terrain outside the protected solver strip remains deterministic procedural infill rather than surveyed and geospatially registered Hance geography.
The cooked hydraulic field is unconverged and uncalibrated against observed Hance behavior across playable releases.

geospatial review of river-mile registration, planform, terrain, bank breaklines, bathymetry, rapid rocks, and vertical datum
hydraulic convergence and calibration against observed Hance behavior across playable discharge bands
geology, ecology, and environment-art approval of strata, boulders, shrubs, grass, ground cover, wet banks, and canyon context
photoreal water/VFX and raft/character-occlusion approval for depth, transmission, foam, spray, mist, reflections, shoreline contact, rafts, and passengers
target-hardware performance, collision, capsize, recovery, and complete-run gameplay acceptance
